report_name: Tensorlake NPM Package Compromised by Shai-Hulud Worm

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The 'tensorlake' npm package was compromised by injecting malicious code into version 0.5.144, which was then published to the public npm registry to be installed by developers.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: The malware was executed via an npm 'preinstall' hook, which ran an obfuscated JavaScript-based payload using the Bun runtime.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: The Shai-Hulud worm deployed the 'HackBrowserData' binary to steal credentials stored in web browsers from compromised developer environments.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The malware specifically searched for and exfiltrated SSH private keys and cryptocurrency wallet keys from compromised developer environments.

attack_patterns.name: Access Token Manipulation
attack_patterns.description: The worm used stolen npm and GitHub access tokens to authenticate to the respective services and automatically republish other packages owned by the victim with the malicious payload.

attack_patterns.name: Application Layer Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The malware used a non-standard C2 mechanism, communicating via an Ethereum smart contract for resilient command and control, with GitHub as a fallback.

attack_patterns.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
attack_patterns.description: The malware utilized an obfuscated loader and obfuscated code within the preinstall script to evade detection and analysis.

malware.name: Shai-Hulud
malware.description: A self-propagating worm delivered via the compromised 'tensorlake' NPM package. It is designed to steal a wide range of developer credentials and uses them to infect other packages, furthering the supply chain attack.

tools.name: HackBrowserData
tools.description: A binary deployed by the Shai-Hulud worm to steal credentials stored in web browsers.

tools.name: Bun
tools.description: A legitimate JavaScript runtime abused by the malware's obfuscated loader to execute the primary payload.

tools.name: npm
tools.description: The package manager used as the distribution vector for the malicious package and as a propagation mechanism by the worm, which uses stolen tokens to publish new infected packages.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.description: The version control system where the initial malicious commit was made. Stolen GitHub tokens were used for propagation, and it also served as a fallback C2 mechanism.

tools.name: Sigstore
tools.description: A technology abused by the worm to generate provenance for maliciously republished packages to make them appear legitimate.

campaigns.name: Shai-Hulud
campaigns.description: A software supply chain attack campaign involving a self-propagating credential-stealing worm that compromises NPM packages to harvest developer secrets and infect other projects.

identities.name: Tensorlake
identities.description: The organization/project whose 'tensorlake' NPM package was compromised and used to distribute the Shai-Hulud worm.

identities.name: npm
identities.description: The public package registry where the compromised version of 'tensorlake' (0.5.144) was published.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: The code hosting platform where the initial malicious commit was made to the 'tensorlake' repository.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
identities.description: One of the cloud service providers whose credentials were targeted for theft by the Shai-Hulud worm.

identities.name: HashiCorp
identities.description: The vendor for HashiCorp Vault, a secrets management tool whose credentials were targeted by the malware.

identities.name: Kubernetes
identities.description: The container orchestration platform whose configuration and credentials were targeted by the malware.

identities.name: Ethereum
identities.description: The public blockchain platform used by the malware for its primary command-and-control infrastructure via a smart contract.

identities.name: Developers
identities.description: The primary victims of the attack, whose environments are compromised upon installing the malicious package, leading to credential theft and further propagation.

infrastructure.name: Shai-Hulud Ethereum C2
infrastructure.description: A decentralized command-and-control infrastructure implemented as an Ethereum smart contract, used by the Shai-Hulud worm for resilient C2 communication.

indicators.name: Suspicious Bun Runtime Execution by Package Manager
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Bun Runtime Execution by Package Manager
id: 2b8c5f1a-6e4d-4f9b-8d1c-7a9b3e2f1a0b
status: experimental
description: Detects the 'bun' runtime being executed by a package manager process, which is highly suspicious and was a TTP in the Shai-Hulud worm attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/tensorlake-npm-package-compromised-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\yarn.cmd'
      - '\pnpm.cmd'
    Image|endswith: '\bun.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the 'bun' runtime being executed by a package manager process, a TTP observed in the Shai-Hulud worm attack.

indicators.name: HackBrowserData Credential Stealer Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: HackBrowserData Credential Stealer Execution
id: 8d1c7a9b-3e2f-4a0b-9c5f-1a6e4d4f9b8d
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of HackBrowserData, a known open-source tool for stealing browser credentials, which was used by the Shai-Hulud worm.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/tensorlake-npm-package-compromised-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1555.003
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\HackBrowserData.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the HackBrowserData credential stealing tool.

indicators.name: Installation of Compromised tensorlake NPM Package
indicators.pattern:
title: Installation of Compromised Tensorlake NPM Package
id: 3e2f1a0b-9c5f-4a6e-8d1c-7a9b4d4f9b8d
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of the compromised version (0.5.144) of the 'tensorlake' npm package, which contained the Shai-Hulud worm.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/tensorlake-npm-package-compromised-to.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-08
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'npm'
      - 'install'
      - 'tensorlake@0.5.144'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects command-line activity corresponding to the installation of the specific malicious 'tensorlake' package version.
